newsitem.title: UK: NatWest Markets says sticking with Eurobonds.
newsitem.headline: NatWest Markets says sticking with Eurobonds.

text.p: NatWest Markets, the investment banking arm of Britain's National Westminster Bank Plc, said on Tuesday it had no intention of pulling out of the Eurobond market.
"We are not pulling out of the Eurobond market," a NatWest spokeswoman told Reuters.
The Financial Times newspaper said on Monday NatWest Markets was expected to cut or close its Eurobond sales and trading arm.

But the NatWest spokeswoman said while the firm was not interested in pursuing unprofitable business, it would continue to concentrate on trading, securitisation and its strength in the sterling corporate bond market.
Asked if NatWest Markets would slim down its Eurobond operation by axing staff, she said the firm had not said anything about cutting back on the number of employees.

On Monday NatWest announced the departure of NatWest Markets chief executive Martin Owen and a review aimed at making the most of areas where it had a competitive advantage, deploying capital in activities where it could achieve better results.

The group also said the 90 million stg losses on interest rate options revealed in February had taken their toll on NatWest Markets' business as a whole and would mean a significant drop in profits in the first half of 1997.
NatWest group chief executive Derek Wanless has taken the helm at NatWest Markets until a replacement is found.

The NatWest Markets spokeswoman declined to comment on newspaper speculation about Owen's successor. She said the firm was looking both internally and externally for the best person to lead the business and an appointment would be made as quickly as possible.
